question: Who among the following organized the “Red Shirts” movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan was a prominent freedom fighter known as the "Frontier Gandhi" for his non-violent opposition to British rule.
 
• He founded the "Red Shirts" movement, also known as the Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God), which was a non-violent resistance movement against British colonial rule in the North-West Frontier Province (now in Pakistan).
 
• The movement aimed to promote social reform and self-reliance among the Pathan people and was inspired by Mahatma Gandhi's principles of non-violence and civil disobedience.
 
• Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1987.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Red Shirts Movement (Khudai Khidmatgar)**

 
 
• The Red Shirts movement was a Pashtun (Pathan) movement against British rule that advocated non-violent protest and social reform.
 
• The members of the movement wore red shirts as a symbol of unity and resistance, which is why they were called "Red Shirts".
 
• The movement was primarily active in the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) and played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The movement also aimed at promoting education, economic development, and social cohesion among the Pathans.
 
 
 
• **Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan**
 
 
• Also known as Bacha Khan or Badshah Khan, he was a senior political and spiritual leader known for his non-violent opposition to British rule.
 
• He was a devout follower of Mahatma Gandhi and his ideals of non-violence (Ahimsa).
 
• He was a key figure in the Indian National Congress and worked closely with other prominent leaders of the Indian independence movement.
 
• After the partition of India, he continued to advocate for the rights of the Pashtun people and opposed the partition.
 
 
 
• **North-West Frontier Province (NWFP)**
 
 
• The NWFP was a province of British India, now part of Pakistan, located along the border with Afghanistan.
 
• The region has a significant Pashtun population and has historically been a center of resistance against foreign rule.
 
• The province played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement and was a stronghold of the Khudai Khidmatgar movement.
 
• After the partition of India in 1947, the NWFP became part of Pakistan and is now known as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
